name: Mexico
seoTitle: History of Mexico: Tenochtitlan, The Aztec Eagle Flag Vexillology, and 1810 Independence
metaDescription: Explore the comprehensive history of Mexico. Discover Tenochtitlan, the Grito de Dolores of 1810, the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, and the 1917 Constitution.
mapFormation:
Bridging North and Central America across 1.97 million square kilometers, the United Mexican States (Estados Unidos Mexicanos) encompasses vast geographic biomes, from the arid Chihuahuan and Sonoran deserts in the north to the Sierra Madre mountain spines, central volcanic plateaus, and tropical rainforests of Chiapas and the Yucatán Peninsula. For over three millennia, Mesoamerican civilizations—including the Olmec, Maya, Zapotec, and Toltec—established sophisticated urban centers and astronomical observatories.

In 1325, the Mexica (Aztec) people founded their imperial island capital of Tenochtitlan in Lake Texcoco. Following the Spanish conquest led by Hernán Cortés in 1521, the territory became the heart of the Viceroyalty of New Spain (Virreinato de la Nueva España), governing territories stretching from California to Costa Rica.

Following independence in 1821 and the dissolution of the short-lived First Mexican Empire, Mexico became a federal republic in 1824. The geopolitical borders were dramatically reshaped during the 19th century: Texas seceded in 1836, and following the Mexican-American War, the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) forced Mexico to cede 55% of its territory (including modern California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Colorado and Wyoming) to the United States. The Gadsden Purchase (1853) and southern border treaties with Guatemala (1882) and British Honduras/Belize (1893) established the modern sovereign frontiers.
flagHistory:
The national flag of Mexico—the Bandera de México—is a magnificent vertical tricolor of green, white, and red, bearing at its center the sacred national coat of arms rooted in ancient Mexica mythology.

The tricolor design was first created in February 1821 during the final campaign of the War of Independence by the Army of the Three Guarantees (Ejército Trigarante), led by royalist-turned-insurgent Agustín de Iturbide and insurgent leader Vicente Guerrero. In the original 1821 Plan of Iguala, Green represented Independence, White symbolized the Catholic Faith, and Red represented the Union between Europeans and indigenous Mexicans. During the 19th-century liberal reforms of President Benito Juárez, the colors were officially secularized: Green represents Hope, White symbolizes Purity and National Unity, and Red honors the Blood of the Fallen Heroes.

At the exact center of the white stripe sits the National Crest, depicting an Eagle perched atop a Prickly Pear Cactus (Nopal) emerging from an islet in Lake Texcoco, clutching a rattlesnake in its talon and beak. According to Aztec prophecy, the god Huitzilopochtli commanded the nomadic Mexica people to build their empire where they witnessed this divine celestial omen, leading to the founding of Tenochtitlan in 1325.
freedomStory:
Mexico's path to sovereign freedom was ignited on the early morning of September 16, 1810, in the town of Dolores, Guanajuato, when parish priest Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla rang the church bells and delivered the immortal Grito de Dolores ('Cry of Dolores'), summoning indigenous and mestizo citizens to rise against three centuries of colonial oppression.

Following Hidalgo's martyrdom, Father José María Morelos assumed leadership, convening the Congress of Chilpancingo in 1813 and drafting the Sentimientos de la Nación ('Sentiments of the Nation'), declaring human rights and the abolition of slavery. After eleven years of guerrilla warfare, insurgent leader Vicente Guerrero and Agustín de Iturbide united forces under the Plan of Iguala, entering Mexico City in triumph and signing the Treaty of Córdoba on August 24, 1821, which sealed Mexican independence from the Spanish Empire.

In the mid-19th century, indigenous Zapotec statesman Benito Juárez enacted the landmark Leyes de Reforma (Reform Laws), separating church and state and defeating the French imperial intervention of Maximilian I in 1867. The subsequent Mexican Revolution of 1910, led by Francisco I. Madero, Emiliano Zapata, and Pancho Villa, culminated in the promulgation of the progressive Constitution of 1917 in Querétaro, the first constitution in global history to enshrine comprehensive labor rights, agrarian reform, and universal public education.
challenges: In the 21st century, Mexico is the second-largest economy in Latin America, a top-15 global economy, and a premier manufacturing hub integrated into the North American trade corridor through the USMCA treaty. Major contemporary priorities include strengthening the rule of law and judicial transparency, combating transnational organized crime networks, and investing in critical logistics infrastructure such as the Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec. Environmentally, Mexico manages severe water scarcity across its industrial northern states and accelerates solar, geothermal, and nearshoring manufacturing modernization.

faqs.question: What was the 'Grito de Dolores' in Mexican history?
faqs.answer: The Grito de Dolores ('Cry of Dolores') was the revolutionary call to arms issued on September 16, 1810, by Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla in Dolores, Guanajuato, marking the beginning of the Mexican War of Independence.

faqs.question: What is the mythological origin of the eagle on the Mexican flag?
faqs.answer: The eagle perched on a nopal cactus devouring a serpent originates from the ancient Aztec prophecy given by Huitzilopochtli, showing the Mexica people where to build their imperial capital of Tenochtitlan in 1325.

faqs.question: What was the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848)?
faqs.answer: Signed on February 2, 1848, the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ended the Mexican-American War, in which Mexico ceded over 50% of its northern territory (including modern California, Nevada, Utah, and Arizona) to the United States for $15 million.

faqs.question: Why is the 1917 Mexican Constitution historically significant worldwide?
faqs.answer: Promulgated in Querétaro following the Mexican Revolution, the 1917 Constitution was the first in world history to enshrine social and labor rights, such as an 8-hour workday, minimum wage, the right to strike, and agrarian land redistribution.

timeline.event: The Mexica establish Tenochtitlan in Lake Texcoco after witnessing the prophecy of the eagle on the cactus.
Spanish conquistadors led by Hernán Cortés capture Tenochtitlan, establishing the Viceroyalty of New Spain.
Father Miguel Hidalgo issues the Grito de Dolores on September 16, sparking the Mexican War of Independence.
The Treaty of Córdoba is signed on August 24, officially recognizing Mexican independence from Spain.
The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo concludes the Mexican-American War, ceding northern territories.
President Benito Juárez defeats the French intervention, restoring the sovereign Mexican Republic.
The Mexican Revolution leads to the promulgation of the landmark 1917 Constitution of Querétaro.
Mexico enters the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), accelerating modern industrialization.
